LESSON: PAINTING AND MONTAGE

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.3: Painting and Montage
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Painting and Montage, part of Creating and Executing in Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How is glue for pasting pictures improvised? 2. Why is colour classification important in painting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. mix primary colours to create secondary colours,

2. mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip,

3. mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip

4. draw a single object and paint with emphasis on colour value,

5. observe sample montage pictures for familiarity,

6. source picture of ball games and cut out,

7. arrange and paste cut-out pictures to make a montage themed “ball games” and clean the working area, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. mix primary colours to create secondary colours,
2. mix white with a secondary colour to create light tones on a scale strip,
3. mix black with a secondary colour to create dark tones on a scale strip
4. draw a single object and paint with emphasis on colour value,
5. observe sample montage pictures for familiarity,
6. source picture of ball games and cut out,
7. arrange and paste cut-out pictures to make a montage themed “ball games” and clean the working area, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Painting and Montage together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups and speaks clearly about their own and others

work.

• Creativity and Imagination: The learner makes thoughtful choices when producing a montage pictorial composition.

Values:
• Respect: The learner accommodates others’ views during critique of their own and others’ painting and montage work.

• Love: The learner takes turns to talk about their own and others work.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: The learner acquires the skill of working with others during creating a montage composition.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: The learner mixes colours in correct proportions to classify as primary or secondary colours.
